executive_summary: Oriental Hotels is now a merger-linked special situation as well as a hotel operating investment. The earlier report omitted the proposed IHCL amalgamation. Operating improvement matters, but the exchange terms, IHCL share price, approvals and completion timetable are central to the equity case.
research_stance: Merger-linked research case: evaluate exchange parity and approval/time risk; use hotel cash flows as a standalone fallback rather than treating a premium P/E in isolation.
results_analysis: September 2026 consolidated sales were ₹117.75 crore, +6.6% YoY and +5.6% QoQ. PAT was ₹8.59 crore, +7.9% YoY and +62.1% QoQ. These percentage changes use the rounded local dataset, so small differences from company-exact growth percentages are expected.

Local operating profit was ₹27.12 crore and OPM 23.03%, compared with 23.82% a year earlier and 21.03% in June 2026. PAT margin was 7.30%. OPM is the dataset’s operating-profit/sales measure, not automatically management-adjusted EBITDA or a segment EBIT margin.

The prior PAT gap is now reconciled using the official statement: standalone PAT was ₹11.62 crore; consolidated PAT before associates and joint ventures was ₹11.77 crore; after associate loss of ₹0.49 crore and joint-venture loss of ₹2.69 crore, final consolidated profit was ₹8.59 crore. The press release rounds its operating-company PAT to ₹12 crore. This is not an unexplained minority-interest mismatch.

FY26 annual CFO was ₹128 crore and free cash flow ₹93 crore. These are annual figures, not September-quarter cash flow. Latest balance-sheet borrowings were ₹114 crore at 2026-09-30; gross borrowings must not be confused with call net debt. Snapshot ROCE 12.10% is an older-period return measure, not a freshly recomputed quarterly return. The generic ₹114 crore funding field approximately includes ₹34.30 crore of leases alongside ₹79.38 crore of conventional borrowings.

thesis_drivers.evidence: The official release identifies seven hotels and three Taj-branded properties. Brand access and asset upgrades can support pricing, but the limited portfolio concentrates property and local-market risk.

valuation.method: Conditional exchange-parity analysis plus standalone hotel/NAV fallback
valuation.assessment: The proposed all-stock exchange makes IHCL price exposure and completion risk central. At matching 12 November 2026 clean closes, gross parity is ₹188.46 versus OHL ₹173.90. This is neither a cash offer nor risk-free arbitrage. Value the failed-deal case using hotel operating cash flow, investments and funding separately.
assumptions: The proposed ratio of 25/117 is not a completed exchange.
Local 12 November closes were IHCL ₹882 and OHL ₹173.90. Gross parity assumes an unchanged IHCL price, successful completion and no costs.
Approval timing, fractional entitlements, dividends, corporate actions and hedging or financing costs can affect the realized payoff.

base: The proposal remains conditional and OHL price tracks both IHCL and the time/approval discount.

Weak hotel productivity and reinvestment requirements reduce failed-deal value.

claim_audit.assessment: 12 November IHCL ₹882 × 25/117 = ₹188.46. OHL at ₹173.90 is 7.73% below parity; gross convergence upside of 8.37% assumes an unchanged IHCL price and successful completion.

claim_audit.claim: A hotel-only valuation framework omits a material driver of the equity payoff.
claim_audit.assessment: Exchange terms and acquirer-price exposure must be considered alongside standalone hotel cash flows as a failed-deal valuation reference.

business_economics: The operating business earns room and ancillary revenue from a concentrated South Indian portfolio supported by IHCL brands. RevPAR growth combines occupancy and rates; revenue growth alone cannot isolate either. Renovation closures, food and beverage activity, and property mix affect how room productivity reaches cash profit.

The shareholder case differs from an unchanged standalone hotel case. The proposed exchange makes both acquirer performance and transaction conditions material. The hotels and strategic investments also support a fallback valuation if implementation does not occur.
earnings_quality: Final consolidated profit includes associates and joint ventures; the press-release highlight uses a different perimeter. The statement-based reconciliation in the results section resolves the earlier unexplained PAT discrepancy.

A hotel cash-flow assessment should separate recurring maintenance, upgrade investment and investment income from operating earnings. Historical cash generation supports liquidity but does not establish the return or cost of every planned upgrade.
capital_allocation: The merger can simplify ownership and give the assets access to a larger capital platform, but investors should test exchange economics and minority treatment rather than assume all synergies accrue to current OHL holders.

Debt and leases need consistent treatment in hotel EV/EBITDA. Adding leases to enterprise value while mixing pre-lease and post-lease earnings measures, or double counting rental costs, distorts comparisons.
valuation_logic: Gross parity equals the acquirer price multiplied by the exchange ratio. A discount may compensate for time, approval risk, failed-deal downside, dividends, transaction costs and inability to hedge. A larger spread is not free profit.
The failed-deal case should value hotel operations and financial interests net of appropriate liabilities. Transaction parity cannot be used as both successful-deal value and failed-deal valuation.
peer_positioning: IHCL is the relevant payoff reference under the exchange proposal. EIH, Chalet and other hotel owners remain operating/NAV comparators, with different ownership and lease profiles. A broad hotel P/E ranking would miss the announced transaction.
